transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-01-31 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (Redwood Product), Jordan Blake (NorthReach Head of ML), Maya Chen (Infra Eng), Priya Iyer (Security), Tom Reeves (SRE), R. Patel (PM)

AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY:
Redwood and NorthReach kickoff to align on implementation scope and pilot runway. Focus on network, security, dedicated capacity considerations and pilot KPIs.

TOPICS: onboarding timeline; VPC peering; KMS/encryption; dedicated vs hosted pilot; observability hooks; SLO/KPI definition

TRANSCRIPT BODY:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick intros?
[00:06] Jordan (NorthReach): Jordan here, head of ML at NorthReach. We're excited to get this moving.
[00:09] Maya (Infra): Maya, infra eng, I'll own VPC and peering setup.
[00:12] Priya (Sec): Priya, security and compliance. I'll track SOC2 and KMS questions.
[00:15] Tom (SRE): Tom, SRE, I'll do scaling and SLA ops.
[00:18] Alex: Great. From Redwood Samira SE, I'll work on the runtime integration and performance. Diego CSM will handle success plan. Nina for product alignment.
[00:27] Samira (SE): Quick agenda — we want to confirm the pilot scope, traffic profile, whether you want hosted API first or straight to Dedicated, and the security constraints for Private/VPC.
[00:36] R. Patel (PM): Our timeline is fairly tight, Q2 roll out. We need a pilot by mid-February to validate latency and cost.
[00:42] Alex: Understood. Jordan, what are your main success criteria? Latency, cost, hallucination rate?
[00:49] Jordan: For us it's latency under 250ms P90 for short inference routes, cost per 1k tokens under the threshold we modelled, and semantic accuracy on our prompt set — like F1 > 0.82 on our evaluation suite. We also need encryption at rest and audit logs for queries.
[01:05] Priya: To add, we need KMS integration and key rotation policy, plus evidence of audit logging for sensitive inference traces. Also data residency in the us-east-1 region.
[01:14] Nina (Product): Also, we'll need function-calling support for structured outputs, so can you confirm that the runtime supports tool-calling and streaming?
[01:21] Samira: Yes, runtime supports streaming and structured outputs, though the kernel path for quantized models may affect latency slightly for complex tool-calls.
[01:28] Maya: Can you explain the network topology for Dedicated and for hosted with VPC peering? We need to understand egress and firewall rules.
[01:36] Samira: For hosted: we offer VPC peering with a secure egress path, you keep the private endpoints. For Dedicated: we provision private GPU pool inside your tenant or our managed tenant depending on the contract; peering is still used and you get IP whitelisting. There is a small NAT egress when using managed KMS unless you bring your own HSM.
[01:54] Tom: How does the KV cache behave across instances? If we shard the model across GPUs, will prefix caching be preserved?
[02:02] Samira: Good question. The runtime manages KV cache sharding — it keeps client session affinity within pool instances; prefix caching works per shard but we also have cross-instance cache warmups for commonly repeated contexts. There might be a warmup lag for a cold start.
[02:20] Jordan: For the pilot we'll probably run northreach-search endpoints with 20 RPS average, spiky to 80 RPS during peak tests.
[02:27] Samira: That's within Dedicated capacity we'd recommend a small pool with autoscale thresholds. For hosted, we can set route-specific quotas to avoid noisy neighbor impact.
[02:35] Alex: Cost guidance — Redwood to provide an estimate for both hosted pilot and dedicated baseline so you can compare. We'll include estimated token spend and GPU slot hours.
[02:45] R. Patel: Who's responsible for the pilot runbook? We want a clear plan for success/fail criteria.
[02:50] Diego (CSM): Diego here — we'll draft the runbook and share a template. We suggest: baseline metrics, traffic generator config, prompts for semantic checks, rollback criteria, and timeline.
[03:03] Priya: On compliance we need to review the SOC2, ISO logos plus procedure for redaction of PII; also can you confirm retention windows for logs in hosted vs dedicated?
[03:12] Alex: Hosted keeps logs in RW-managed retention by default 30 days, adjustable as an add-on. Dedicated gives you longer retention and options for audit export to your S3 via KMS. We'll send the retention matrix.
[03:24] Tom: Any special routing if we hit capacity issues? Do you have automatic fallback to cheaper model variants?
[03:30] Samira: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible quantized variants or lower-capacity tier to maintain availability. That said, for the pilot we'll likely pin a model to avoid quality regressions.
[03:42] Jordan: We need to keep quality consistent — fallbacks are fine only if they pass the semantic suite thresholds.
[03:48] Nina: Observability — can the console stream token-level latency for routes and tie to a trace id?
[03:53] Samira: Yes, per-route traces with token-level breakdown are in Console; we can wire your Datadog/NewRelic via webhooks or export traces to your APM.
[04:02] Maya: For peering, what ports do you need open? We prefer a minimal set.
[04:06] Samira: We'll provide a list but typically you need outbound to Redwood control plane on 443 and ingress from Redwood to a managed endpoint range on tls/443. If you use SFTP or artifact pulling we will give specific ports.
[04:17] Priya: KMS integration: do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, and HSM for on-prem?
[04:22] Alex: Customer-managed KMS keys are supported for Dedicated and Private. HSM integration is available for Private/on-prem with the enterprise tier.
[04:30] Jordan: Can we run an initial benchmark? We want latency profiles at sequence lengths 32, 128 and 512 tokens across our representative prompts.
[04:36] Samira: Absolutely. We'll run a perf bench. Action: Samira will draft the bench plan with exact prompt samples and request endpoints.
[04:45] Tom: Any throttling policies during pilot? We can't have noisy neighbor affect production trials.
[04:49] Samira: We'll suggest route-level throttles and quotas, plus a dedicated pool option to guarantee capacity.
[04:55] Diego: On success criteria again — let's capture the top three pilot KPIs: 1) P90 latency <= 250ms (seq<=128), 2) semantic F1 >= 0.82 on evaluation set, 3) error rate < 0.5% over 24h test window. Agree?
[05:12] Jordan: Agree.
[05:13] R. Patel: Timeline check — we need SOW and pricing by Feb 3 to get procurement moving.
[05:18] Alex: We'll aim to get SOW and cost sheet by Feb 3.
[05:20] Priya: Also please include audit perf for encryption, and a section on data deletion and redaction.
[05:27] Nina: Regarding structured outputs — do you support function-calling with schema validation hooks?
[05:32] Samira: We have structured output support and optional strict schema validation for responses; we can enable a validation pipeline in the runtime or in the client SDK.
[05:42] Jordan: For the evaluation harness — can Redwood run the prompt set and provide a per-prompt scorecard?
[05:47] Samira: Yes, we can run the evals and attach diff views, and highlight regressions. We'll keep the evaluation harness reproducible in a repo.
[05:56] Tom: Any suggested staging pattern? We prefer to run a small canary then scale.
[06:00] Diego: We propose a 3-stage approach: staging (sanity), canary with 10% traffic, and full pilot ramp.
[06:06] Maya: Will we need to provide sample credentials for the perf tests?
[06:09] Alex: Yes, you'll provide a temp test key and VPC details. We'll give a minimal set of service accounts.
[06:15] Jordan: One more — on-prem option down the road? We might need private deployment if regulators push.
[06:19] Alex: Private on-prem is possible but longer lead time. We'll scope that in the SOW as an optional future phase.
[06:25] Priya: Could you send the security whitepaper and a contact for SOC2 evidence?
[06:29] Alex: I'll attach the security pack and an evidence checklist.
[06:33] Samira: For benchmarks I'll need representative prompt corpus and expected sequences; Jordan, is that something you can upload to the shared drive?
[06:40] Jordan: Yes, we'll drop the prompt set in the folder by end of day Friday.
[06:44] Nina: On function-calling performance — we want to ensure sub-300ms for common 3-field responses.
[06:50] Samira: We'll include function-call microbenchmarks.
[06:54] Tom: Regarding observability, will Redwood push alerts into our PagerDuty?
[06:57] Diego: Yes, we'll work with your PagerDuty integration, map severity to escalation policies.
[07:02] R. Patel: Okay next steps recap?
[07:04] Alex: Redwood: send SOW and pricing (Alex), perf bench plan (Samira), security pack (Alex). NorthReach: VPC details (Maya), prompt set + eval metrics (Jordan), SOC2 questions (Priya).
[07:13] Priya: I'll compile SOC2 Qs and share by Tuesday.
[07:16] Jordan: We'll target pilot kickoff the week of Feb 15 pending procurement.
[07:20] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the runbook walkthrough.
[07:25] Meeting ended.

NOTES: transcription contains minor mis-recognitions around product names; speaker labels may be approximate.
